lines.en: The streets the monsters had retreated from were little more than ruins.
The logo of a collapsed news organization lay trampled on the ground. The statues of King Sejong the Great and Yi Sunsin, symbols of Gwanghwamun, had been utterly destroyed.
The civilization Seoul had prided itself on had collapsed, and its culture was lost. Only a story remained, but none of the people left in Gwanghwamun had wanted that story.
Watching a few Hwarang go down to dig in the earth, Lee Jihye spoke.
“······Is he really dead?”
But no one answered. Each had a different reason for their silence.
Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung.
They each had their own thoughts, but none could bring themselves to say them aloud.
For fear those thoughts might be wrong.
For fear······ those thoughts might be right.
“No······. Really?”
Kim Dokja's body had been found about an hour after the eighth scenario ended.
“Ajusshi! Come on, wake up! You're joking, right?”
The cause of death: excessive blood loss.
At first, everyone was bewildered.
Kim Dokja, who had been nowhere to be seen throughout the whole affair, was suddenly dead.
Even so, his companions waited without panicking too much.
This had happened a few times before.
When they had first hunted a fire dragon.
And when they had faced the Disaster of Floods.
Kim Dokja had died and come back to life.
So they waited this time, too.
Of course he would come back to life as he always did, look at his companions with that familiar grin, and crack a slightly timid, silly joke.
But Kim Dokja did not get up again.
An hour passed, then two.
At last, a day passed. Even when night fell on the second day.
Kim Dokja did not get up.
And his body grew cold.
Unable to bear watching any longer, Min Jiwon urged his dazed companions into action and had a coffin made.
“······He was the strongest person in Seoul.”
She alone began what no one else had done, what no one else could do.
Something she could do because, although she had known Kim Dokja, her ties to him had been slight.
Min Jiwon made Kim Dokja's sacrifice known.
While everyone had been enthralled by the clash between the strongest, the person who was truly the strongest had quietly chosen death alone. She spread his story.
Everyone called Kim Dokja by a different nickname.
In fact, when the dokkaebi had announced the strongest person, that nickname had sounded different to each listener.
King of a Kingless World.
Lone Messiah.
Ugliest King······.
They had heard different words, but those words all pointed to the same thing.
The strongest person in the Seoul Dome was Kim Dokja, and Kim Dokja had died for Seoul.
Seoul had been saved by Kim Dokja.
A savior who had died where no one knew what he had done.
Min Jiwon made a coffin for that Kim Dokja.
Tears welled in some people's eyes as they watched Kim Dokja's body being laid in the coffin. Others were bewildered, asking who he was, and some sighed after finally hearing his story.
And Shin Yoosung was crying.
“Ajusshi······.”
“Yoosung.”
Jung Heewon drew Shin Yoosung away from the coffin. Lee Hyunsung still looked confused, while Lee Gilyoung wore a blank expression, as though retreating from reality.
“There's no way Dokja-hyung is dead.”
And Lee Jihye cried out in anguish, her fists clenched.
“······Where did Master go?”
“Master can save this ajusshi! Where was Seolhwa-unnie?”
But Yoo Joonghyuk was already gone, unable to hear her reproaches.
At last, bitter tears welled in Lee Jihye's eyes, too.
“Ajusshi is······.”
What she had not wanted to accept, she now had to accept.
Kim Dokja was dead, and he would never come back to life again.
[A new main scenario will begin soon.]
They now had to live in a world without Kim Dokja.
「They now had to live in a world without Kim Dokja.」
If this were ‘Ways of Survival’, there would definitely have been some sentence like that.
“Hmm, to think you'd grieve this much for me.”
I wanted to say that, but no voice came out.
I had neither vocal cords nor a mouth.
At least I could take comfort in watching events through ‘Third-Person Observer's Viewpoint’ whenever my mental energy recovered like this.
It would have been nice to use ‘First-Person Viewpoint’, but it wasn't working at the moment, perhaps because I had identified too deeply with Yoo Joonghyuk.
[Use of ‘First-Person Viewpoint’ is restricted due to excessive immersion.]
Before long, as dirt began to cover the coffin, a few people shouted.
“O Ugliest King!”
Goddammit. Had those dokkaebi bastards really given me a nickname like that?
It had to be that bastard Bihyung's doing.
Watching Shin Yoosung toss flowers to me through her tears, I felt stranger and stranger.
My companions now seemed to accept that I was dead.
Watching my own funeral while alive. I was probably the only person who'd ever done that.
“Hyuuuuuuung―!”
Even Lee Gilyoung, who had kept pretending to be calm until the very end, rushed at the coffin once it was half covered in dirt, tears and snot streaming down his face. Lee Jihye was no better.
“Ajusshiiiiii―!”

The kid who was always snapping at me was making such a fuss because I'd died······ It was touching, I had to admit. It would be quite a sight if I burst straight through the coffin and stood up right now.
But I couldn't do that yet. I was in what people called a ‘cooldown’.
[The benefit of the attribute ‘Eight Lives’ is active.]
I wasn't particularly worried about the resurrection itself.
‘Eight Lives’, the attribute I had gained in [Peace Land] in exchange for ‘King of No Killing’.
This attribute, obtainable only by drinking liquor brewed from the Star Blood and flesh gained by killing the constellation [Yamata no Orochi], literally granted its user ‘Eight Lives’.
[Sacrificing the serpent's first head.]
[This head's ability is ‘Popularity (人望)’.]

A different ability lay dormant in each of [Yamata no Orochi]'s heads, and upon resurrection, the user could receive a blessing related to that ability. Put that way, it wasn't bad. The problem was that resurrection through this benefit required a waiting period, unlike ‘King of No Killing’.
[Resurrection requires a waiting period of 72 hours.]
[Remaining waiting time : 24:07:12]
Another whole day to go······ The next scenario would be starting soon.
I watched my funeral a little longer, then changed viewpoints. Somehow, I felt that if I kept watching, I'd feel too guilty to come back to life.
[Changing the character observed through ‘Third-Person Observer's Viewpoint’.]
A new screen appeared.
A basement with an old-fashioned interior.
A man and a woman were there.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi?”
The woman was, of course, Yoo Sangah.
And needless to say, the person who had freed her from the bonds restraining her limbs until a moment ago was Yoo Joonghyuk.
He was probably honoring the final request I had left him before leaving his body.
“What happened to Dokja-ssi?”
“Kim Dokja is dead.”

At Yoo Joonghyuk's blunt declaration, Yoo Sangah looked as though the world had ended. For some reason, her expression made my heart ache a little. It seemed Kim Dokja's 28 years hadn't been entirely worthless.
“But he'll come back to life.”
“······He'll come back? How······.”
“I don't know how. But there's no way he'd die like that.”
Of course, Yoo Joonghyuk had seen me come back to life with his own eyes before. Even after years had passed, that guy would surely still believe I'd come back.
“······No, he has to come back.”
But why was he clenching his fist?
After a brief silence, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke to the stunned Yoo Sangah.
“Where is Kim Dokja's family?”
His words startled me.
This bastard was even trying to do things I hadn't asked him to?
At the word ‘family’, worry clouded Yoo Sangah's face.
She seemed to have something urgent to tell him.
“His mother······.”
Unfortunately, the screen went dark at that moment, and a message sounded.
[Your mental energy has been completely depleted.]
[‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’ Stage 3 is ending.]

This was the downside of being a soul body. Once spent, mental energy recovered slowly. Perhaps that was only natural without a physical body. A spiritual soul, hon (魂), without its corporeal soul, baek (魄), was like a battery missing one electrode. The longer it went without a body, the more the mind deteriorated. Ghosts went mad for much the same reason.
‘Did Nirvana kill my mother?’
That was why I, too, had to keep desperately asking questions to keep from going mad.
‘Probably not.’
This was my mother we were talking about, not just anyone.
And Nirvana wasn't the sort to kill or torture someone so readily, either. At least while acting as the ‘Leader of the Salvation Church’, Nirvana had a certain gentlemanly side.
But Nirvana's last words troubled me.
They had said my mother was keeping a secret from me.
A secret my mother had been hiding from me?
No matter how hard I thought, I couldn't begin to guess.
······I didn't know.
No, perhaps I didn't want to know.
That was when an indirect message came.
[The constellation ‘Master of Abydos’ is calling your soul.]
I was a little taken aback, since I hadn't heard any indirect messages for a while.
······Master of Abydos?
I carefully recalled the contents of ‘Ways of Survival’.
If I remembered correctly, Abydos referred to the capital of ancient Egypt.
[The nebula <Papyrus> wishes to bestow a ‘Revival (甦生) Story’ upon you.]
······Oh, what's this?
<Papyrus> was the nebula of Egyptian mythology.
[The constellation ‘Scribe of Heaven’ is calling your soul.]
Huh? Metatron, too?
No sooner had I thought that than the next message appeared.
[The nebula <Eden> wishes to guide you along ‘Messiah’s Path’.]
A Revival Story, and a Messiah······?
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ wishes to take you under his wing as a subordinate constellation.]
[The nebula <Olympus> is preparing a place for you.]
······Well, look at that.
[The constellation ‘Master of December 25th’ is calling you.]
[The nebula <Vedas> wishes to give you ‘Feast of Resurrection’.]
[The constellation ‘Flower Warden of Seocheon Flower Fields’ is calling your soul.]
[The nebula <Tamna> wants you.]
Indian mythology, and even Korean mythology?
Countless other messages were pouring in, one after another.
From enormous nebulas to tiny ones, countless nebulas were sending me offers.
Looking at them, I thought I could see what these guys were up to.
So they wanted to drape their own myths over me?
[Some constellations are pointing accusing fingers at one another.]
[Some constellations warn against stealing other people's myths.]
Dionysus, Mithra, Hallakgungi······.
The constellations that had just called me were all connected to ‘resurrection’.
[The constellations are vying over your resurrection.]
In other words, these bastards were scheming to get a stake in my Story.
Every Story grew stronger through being widely told (膾炙).
The more mortals repeated and passed down a Story, the greater its influence became.
But what if, one day, a fellow named ‘Kim Dokja’ rose from his grave after 3 days and shouted the following······?
“I am Kim Dokja! May Christ's blessings be upon you all!”
It didn't matter if Mithra or Dionysus took Christ's place.
People would fall over in shock, and the myth would be reenacted on the spot.
The astonished incarnations would spread the tale, and the Story's reach would surpass all imagination.
As a result, the nebula associated with that Story would gain enormous probability and the power to interfere with the scenarios.
That was precisely why the nebulas were making such a fuss.
My resurrection alone had suddenly given me the power to sway the scenarios.
[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula are watching your choice closely.]
My choice would change the fortunes of the nebulas on the Korean Peninsula.
At first glance, I seemed to hold the upper hand as ‘Party A’, but it was hardly a comfortable position.
[The constellations are vying over the legitimacy of their myths.]
I might seem to have the choice now, but the problem would come after I made it.
‘Resurrection Stories’ were a sensitive subject among the nebulas because of plagiarism disputes.
The rivalry between <Eden> and <Vedas> was particularly fierce, and choosing one carelessly could leave me completely at odds with the other.
I was still only a sprout who hadn't even become a constellation.
But if I turned them all down, I might end up earning everyone's resentment······.
[Many constellations want you to make your choice quickly.]
Damn it.
I was already dreading my companions' reproaches after I came back to life. One wrong move, and I'd become the constellations' public enemy, too.
What should I do······.
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ is mediating the dispute between the constellations.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ emphasizes that what matters is the incarnation's own choice.]
Unexpectedly, Persephone took my side.
But why was this lady helping me?
[Some constellations are displeased with the intervention of ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’.]
[Some constellations ask ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ for a solution.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ recommends inviting the incarnation ‘Kim Dokja’ to the ‘banquet’.]
······Banquet?
And a little later.
[The nebula <Eden> agrees to the proposal of ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’.]
[The nebula <Vedas> agrees to the proposal of ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’.]
[Many constellations agree to the proposal of ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’.]
Somehow, it felt as though I had been sold off cheaply without any say in the matter.
As I savored that strangely hollow feeling, the dokkaebi Youngki suddenly rushed in.
[Huff, huff. Dokja, sir.]
Youngki hovered in the air, sweating profusely, apparently having come in a hurry.
[There's somewhere you need to go.]
[I-it will probably help you to go. I'll make the preparations right away!]
I had a rough idea of where he wanted me to go.
Given how nervous he was, the constellations must have put considerable pressure on him.
Huh? I felt myself float up, and a body began to form.
It wasn't resurrection. It was closer to my soul body taking on a shape. I was still a wandering spirit (浮游靈), but a temporary form had been fashioned for me.
[Hmm. Well, it's an important occasion······.]
A dress shirt and suit with a warm texture appeared and slipped around my naked soul body, which was bare even of genitals. The fabric felt as though it had been made for me.
[Old stories glitter in the distant night sky.]
[<The Constellations' Banquet> is currently being held.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ has invited you to <The Constellations' Banquet> as her partner.]
<The Constellations' Banquet>.

An event arranged for the constellations of the <Star Stream>, alongside <Sponsor Selection>. I had been invited to a banquet reserved for constellations, despite not yet having attained constellationhood.
I checked the time remaining until my resurrection.
[Remaining waiting time : 23:54:12]
23 hours.
There was plenty of time for a brief visit.
It was a little early, but this was definitely somewhere I would have to go at least once.
“All right, let's go.”
At last, the time had come to meet the constellations.
[The person who invited you will send an envoy shortly.]
“Got it.”
[I-I wish you a successful debut!]
Youngki clenched his fist with determination in his eyes, then vanished before me. Looking around, I found the entire area covered in pure white clouds.
I realized this was the ‘Cloud Road’, one of the tributaries connecting the <Star Stream>.
Countless dokkaebis traveled along this road between dimensions.
[You have temporarily left the main scenario area.]
[You must return to the scenario within 24 hours of Earth time.]
[If you fail to return within the allotted time, you will be disposed of according to scenario regulations.]
‘Disposed of’, huh.
Just like when I'd gone to the Underworld last time, the system really had a chilling way with words.
[Hidden Scenario ― ‘The Constellations' Banquet’ is beginning!]
<Hidden Scenario ― The Constellations' Banquet>
Category : Hidden
Difficulty : ?
Clear conditions : Attend the banquet and make a successful debut.
Time limit : 24 hours
Reward : 100000 coins, the goodwill or contempt of some constellations
Upon failure : ―
······Honestly, the <Star Stream> had hidden scenarios tucked away in every imaginable place. If you were determined enough, there were more places to mine coins than you might think.
Keeeeeeen!

I saw four horses flying toward me in the distance. Magnificent steeds that radiated pure white light as though they were light sources. The horses beat their ‘golden wings’ vigorously and snorted with all their might, pulling a carriage that likewise boasted a golden exterior.
A sun symbol was carved into the outside of the carriage.
I recognized the carriage at a glance.
Could that be the ‘Sun Chariot’?
Then the being inside that chariot would be······.
[Hey, get in.]
The sudden, unceremonious True Voice (眞言) startled me.
But the being inside the chariot spoke as though it were nothing.
[Hey, hey, it's fine. From here on, we're in the symbolic realm (象徵界), so the restrictions on True Voice are weaker. Don't be scared. Hurry up and come in. I won't eat you.]
Nervously, I opened the chariot's curtain. If this really was the Sun Chariot, its owner would probably be Helios, the sun god······ Huh?
“Who are you······?”
I looked at the chariot's passenger in puzzlement. To be precise, what was inside wasn't a ‘passenger’.
Only a wineglass brimming with appetizing red wine floated inside the chariot.
As I wondered what on earth was going on, the wineglass spoke.
[What, you don't recognize me?]
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ feels hurt by you.]
Startled, I asked.
“······Dionysus?”
Tzzzzzt!
Dazzling sparks flew, and the wineglass screamed in pleasure.
[Hey, you shouldn't throw a true name around like that. Though the tingles do feel good.]
“······Why do you look like that?”
[Probability, what else? A symbolic form like this is good for cutting costs. As you know, the great <Star Stream> is pretty strict.]
Actually, it was better for me if he wasn't in his true body, either.
Even with [Fourth Wall], I still wasn't sure I could look at a constellation's true body and remain sane.
The chariot set off as soon as I sat down.
I didn't know why Dionysus was driving the Sun Chariot of the Titan god Helios, but there seemed to be a reason.
[This is our first time meeting in person, right? Nice to meet you. I'm the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’. In your country, I'm famous as the name of a fatigue remedy.]
“It's nice to meet you, too.”
After exchanging awkward greetings, we sat in separate corners of the chariot.
Unlike his usual playful manner, Dionysus wasn't very talkative.
Was he unexpectedly shy around strangers?
I hadn't expected that. Still, the Stories couldn't all be accurate.

More than that, the wine sloshing around in his glass whenever the chariot jolted was really bothering me. He wasn't going to suddenly spill it on me, was he? That liquid had to be a symbol of something, too. What part of Dionysus did it represent?
After I'd spent a little while on such pointless thoughts, Dionysus spoke.
[Oh, sorry. I was chatting with a goddess I know.]
“······You must be very busy?”
[Not really, but we've got a little something going on these days, so I have to keep her interested.]
I couldn't tell whether he was serious or joking.
[But you're calmer than I expected. I am a constellation, you know.]
“This isn't my first time seeing a constellation.”
[Oh, come to think of it, you're right. I sent you to the Underworld last time, didn't I?]
“Thank you for that.”
[No need to thank me. More to the point, what did you get up to in the Underworld?]
“Pardon?”
[I've never seen that haughty queen act so kindly. Taking on the nebulas to protect a single incarnation, no less······ Huh? Could it be? Is that it? You and that lady······.]
His voice sounded oddly envious. Dionysus didn't seem to know that I had carried out Persephone's task.
“Nothing happened.”
[Hey, hey, don't play dumb. She's fucking sexy, isn't she? If she didn't have a husband, I'd have tried something with her ages ago······.]
“······Is it all right for you to talk like that? Isn't the Queen of the Underworld your mother?”
[Hmm? Haha. There is that version, yes.]
“Was that version false, then?”
[I didn't say that.]
[What's that look for? Don't you know Olympus? A taboo like this is nothing.]
Come to think of it, Olympus was that sort of place.
A paradise for gods who thought with their crotches.
Even so, wasn't this going a bit far?

[Oh, right. Good thing you brought it up. You got my message earlier, didn't you? Come over to my side. I'll bestow the ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’ Story on you as a special favor······ You don't look too pleased?]
“That's not it.”
I hurriedly shook my head.
As one of the twelve Olympian gods, Dionysus was a constellation of high Status.
But merely ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’······.
[Aha, I get it. Look at you. You were comparing it with the Stories <Eden> and <Vedas> are offering, weren't you?]
“Not particularly, but······.”

[You idiot, that's because you don't know any better! Do you know what happens if you receive a Story like ‘Resurrected Messiah’? You have to live your entire life as a virgin! And after you die, too. Huh? You have to serve the creator god without ever getting to fuck!]
Dionysus shouted excitedly.
[Huh? Now, do you know how amazing ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’ is by comparison? You know my female followers, right?]
“You mean the female followers who tore a homosexual person to pieces and killed them?”
Dionysus flinched.

[Uh······ Ahem. Y-yes! You can spend every night with them in a frenzy. And y-you get unlimited refills of the wine I bestow! Think that's all? Ever heard of an ‘Olympus Orgy Party’? You know Aphrodite, right? If you want, I could invite her, too······.]
[The constellation ‘Goddess of Love and Beauty’ glares at ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’.]
[······Forget what I said about her. Anyway, what do you think?]
“It doesn't really appeal to me.”
Dionysus's wine sloshed uneasily.
[······Come to think of it, a certain angel from <Eden> said you were a lover of men······ ]
“I think I know who spread that rumor, but I like women. More to the point, I'd like to hear the real reason you came to see me.”
[Hmm? What do you mean? Obviously, to bring you into our nebula······.]
“Is that really all?”
Dionysus was silent for a moment.
The wineglass, which had been sloshing for some time, spun once in the air.
[······You're sharp.]
“I get that a lot.”
[Want a drink? Have some of my wine.]
“I'm not very fond of alcohol.”
[Well······ All right. You're right. The truth is, I'm not here to bring you into ‘Olympus’.]
Just as I'd thought.

He had rattled on about goddesses and whatnot, but he hadn't meant any of it. No matter how many nebulas had their eyes on me, it had been strange from the start that one of the twelve major Olympian gods had come to pick up a mere incarnation.
But Dionysus's next words completely overturned my expectations.
[I'll get straight to the point. I don't want you to join ‘Olympus’.]
“······Pardon?”
[To be more precise······.]
That was when a terrible explosion rang out.
KABOOOOM!
The Sun Chariot lurched as though struck by artillery, and the horses at the front screamed. Looking back, I saw that wine had spilled from Dionysus's glass.
[Aaagh, fuck. I pissed myself from the shock!]
I was afraid to ask what, exactly, was piss.
I scrambled desperately to avoid touching the spilled wine.
[Damn it, looks like other nebulas are after you.]

Looking outside the curtain, I saw things radiating an overwhelming presence flying toward us from every direction. They were still too far away to tell which nebula they belonged to, but they clearly weren't friendly.

[Fuck. I paid that bastard Helios a fortune to rent this······ Hey, this won't work. I'll drop you off here, so run the rest of the way. Follow the Cloud Road straight ahead, and you'll be there in no time.]
Here? In midair?
[I'll hold them off, so hurry! Once you reach the banquet hall, no nebula can touch you!]
With those words, the curtain flew open.
I swallowed as I looked at the floor of clouds far below.
I was a soul. So even if I fell, I wouldn't die.
Dionysus's voice came from behind me.
[Remember. Trust no one.]
As I leaped from the chariot, Dionysus spoke with a grin.
[See you again, incarnation Kim Dokja.]
I jumped straight out of the chariot.
Tzzzzzt!
KABOOOOOM!

An enormous explosion resounded behind me, and an overwhelming presence pressed against my entire body. It was a tremendous power unlike anything I had felt before. At least part of a true body seemed to have descended.
Rrrrrrumble!
CRRRRASH!
Sparks struck like thunder.
I knew without looking back.
A battle between constellations had clearly begun.
I ran along the Cloud Road with all my might. Something like debris skimmed over my head, and it felt as though the ground was splitting beneath me. Still, I didn't look back.
How long had I been running?
At last, an enormous fortress came into view, and the noise behind me subsided.
I reached the entrance to the fortress.
“I've come to attend the banquet.”
The gatekeeper looked me up and down.
It appeared to be a low-ranking dokkaebi dispatched by the Bureau.
“What's this? I didn't hear anything about an incarnation coming.”
Damn it. Getting out of the Sun Chariot seemed to have been a mistake.
That had probably been my ticket straight in.
Just then, a door inside the fortress opened, and an unexpected savior appeared.
[Let that fellow in. He's with me.]
It wasn't Persephone.
A constellation I had long wanted to see was waiting for me there.
He stood at the entrance to the banquet hall.
If I was right, he was one of the few high-ranking constellations who had consistently supported me since the early scenarios.

「A face framed by brilliant white-gold fur, wearing a mischievous expression. A prisoner confined in the world's smallest prison as punishment for making a mockery of the most exalted throne. No one could help drawing a sharp breath upon meeting his noble Fiery Golden Eyes (火眼金睛).」

He really was exactly as ‘Ways of Survival’ had described him. I gazed at him as though spellbound. A being at the very pinnacle of the Narrative-grade constellations in ‘Ways of Survival’. Ignoring the gatekeeper, I rushed inside.
“Great Sage, Heaven's Equal!”
But with a mischievous smile, the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, vanished before my eyes.
Like smoke.
As though to say I wasn't yet worthy of meeting him.
······Was that a clone?
Dejected, I lowered my outstretched hand, but that wasn't the end of it.
Having entered while repeatedly calling out the name of the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, I had suddenly drawn the attention of the constellations on the first floor of the banquet hall.
[Who's that guy?]
An incarnation entering while calling out a particular constellation's nickname.
There was no way most constellations would take kindly to that.
Gazes poured toward me from all over the banquet hall.
[He's an incarnation?]
[What? Whose incarnation is he?]
As countless gazes converged on me, the air instantly began to boil, and my body went so rigid I couldn't move.
The gathering gazes made my mind go blank. I couldn't even tell who was looking at me.
I had thought I could now endure hearing the constellations' True Voices. But it became clear that this had been entirely due to [Fourth Wall].
To end up like this just from being looked at.
Only then did it truly sink in.
Right now, I was the only being in this banquet hall who wasn't a constellation.
At last, I stood before the constellations.
“Now, now, please calm down, constellation-nims. There's been a little mix-up, so I'll be taking this fellow away.”

I thought I heard a familiar voice, and then someone hoisted my rigid soul body up and began carrying me somewhere. Once we left the murmuring banquet hall and entered a corridor, that hell of staring eyes ended, and I could finally breathe.
“······Why the hell did you come alone?”
I raised my head at the voice, and sure enough, a familiar figure was bobbing in the air.
“Bihyung?”
“Yeah, it's me. The Queen of the Night said she'd send an envoy. Didn't you come with them? Why are you wandering around the wrong place by yourself? Trying to get yourself killed?”
“Something came up.”
“Hey, you can't just brush this off like that! This isn't a scenario area, you bastard! Get cocky here, and you're dead! This place······.”
“Is full of beings who can kill humans like bugs with a glance.”
I knew.
I knew very well.
That was why I'd come here.
Bihyung jutted out his lips in displeasure, then led me somewhere.
“I'll take you to the waiting room, so rest there for a while. There's a screen in there, so make sure you watch it. You have to watch, got it?”
Judging by the way he was swaggering, something good seemed to have happened to him. Before long, I reached the waiting room.
But the sign on the waiting room was, well, rather peculiar.
“······<Incarnation Waiting Room>? There's such a thing?”
“You think you're the only incarnation here? ······Of course, you're the only bastard who barged in alone.”

“His nickname is······.”

······Beg a Historical-grade for a Story?

<Story Inheritance Ceremony>.

We walked into the banquet hall one by one.

[Selena Kim! King's Guardian!]
[I've been following your exploits!]

Their excited demeanor, as though they'd met their favorite celebrities.

She seemed to be saying something like this.
「See that?」
······So what?
At last, it was my turn.

The atmosphere, so heated a moment ago, went quiet as though someone had doused it with cold water.
······Was I not very popular?

[Kim Dokja! That guy is the Kim Dokja]

Incarnations dying amid screams, and constellations snickering as they watched.

[Have you heard of ‘Goryeo's First Sword’? I hear his legends have been circulating widely again lately.]
Goryeo's First Sword.

Yellow ceremonial robes and a sacred scripture (聖典) floating behind.

At my command, the self-proclaimed Founder of Humanity vanished in a flash of white light, flustered and shouting something or other.
You should have behaved while you had the chance.

Even if my counterpart was ‘Narrative-grade’, I had no intention of groveling under the weight of his aura. Things might be different after the Story inheritance was complete, but for now, I was ‘Party A’, the one with the upper hand.
“Next.”
No sooner had I spoken than someone opened the door and appeared.
A wanderer wearing an old crown and threadbare clothes. Who was this?
[Incarnation Kim Dokja, join <Olympus>.]
Had these bastards all read some ‘Kim Dokja Instruction Manual’ before coming here?
[The constellation ‘The One Who Stabbed His Own Eyes’ smiles at you.]
······The One Who Stabbed His Own Eyes?
[You seem to know me.]
“In my country, once someone becomes a university student, they hear your story until they're sick of it.”
[Is that so? How unexpected. In a small country in the East······.]
‘The One Who Stabbed His Own Eyes’. He was ‘King Oedipus’, taught ad nauseam in university general-education courses. My hatred for Sophocles welled up again for the first time in a while.
“Anyway, I've already heard your proposal from the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’. You've come to tell me to become the ‘Cult Leader of Bacchus’, haven't you?”
[Bacchus? So he has already approached you.]
Something felt off.
Come to think of it, Persephone, who was attending the banquet, was at odds with ‘Olympus’, and Dionysus had told me to ‘trust no one’.
And neither of them had told me to join <Olympus>.
Yet King Oedipus had opened with precisely that.
[I have not come to make Bacchus's proposal. Much less to exercise copyright over a ‘resurrection Story’.]
In other words, King Oedipus had come to make me an offer completely different from those of the two previous constellations.
······Perhaps this was the ‘real’ representative of Olympus?
[The Story <Olympus> offers you is ‘Carnival of Lightning’.]
“What?”
I was startled. ‘Carnival of Lightning’ was the Story of Zeus, one of the three chief gods.
Seeing my expression, Oedipus gave a curious smile.
[As expected, you seem to know this Story. Yes, you're right. The Story we offer is on an entirely different level of Status from the resurrection Stories of other ‘nebulas’.]
“······Why are you making me such an offer?”
[Because the Three Goddesses of Fate and I have seen a fragment of your fate.]
······My fate?

[Soon, you will become qualified to inherit ‘Carnival of Lightning’. Of course, you could inherit my Story and receive ‘Blind Prophet’ instead······ But since you are already rumored to be a prophet, you probably won't inherit my Story.]
“Wait. What do you mean? Why would I have that sort of fate······.”
[The decision is yours. But you will certainly come to need <Olympus>. Think carefully until we meet again.]
With those final words, Oedipus vanished from the room.
I felt a little unsettled.
I didn't know what ‘fate’ Oedipus meant, but if the Three Goddesses of Fate were involved, something resembling the future they'd seen would happen to me in the near future.
But an event that would qualify me to inherit a Greek Story, of all things? I couldn't help feeling uneasy. The Stories from that lot were all······.
[Hi?]

I thought I saw a head suddenly poke in, and before I knew it, someone had entered the room. A fresh, sweet fragrance. A beautiful angel's face was right before mine. A youthful, girl-like angel who brought a little devil (小惡魔) to mind.
Apparently, it was <Eden>'s turn.
“······I thought the ‘Master of the Ark’ would come, but you've come yourself.”
[Are you disappointed it's me?]
Hearing her voice suddenly turn despondent, I feel my heart sink.
······To think that ‘Uriel’ was this cute.
“No, I'm glad to see you.”
[I missed you, Kim Dokja!]

Uriel practically ambushed me with a tight hug. As our bodies pressed together, I felt an unholy sensation through the thin silk she wore. A devil······ This was the touch of a devil. Since her dress left her back bare, my hands suddenly had nowhere to go. Uriel rubbed her face against my chest as though she'd found an adorable doll, and I answered with something like a sigh.
“I······ missed you, too.”
[Mm-hmm! Mm-hmm!]
It was a slightly awkward situation, but meeting her was deeply moving for me, too.
Uriel was a constellation who had stayed with me ever since the moment the scenarios began.
“You've come to tell me to choose ‘Messiah's Path’, haven't you?”
[······Oh, right! That's why I came!]
Startled, Uriel lifted her head from my chest.
She didn't look like she'd remembered at all.
She must have been awfully happy to see me.
[I guess it's because you're so handsome.]
“That's a very convincing explanation.”
Uriel gave a bright smile and spoke.
[Kim Dokja, you'll accept our <Eden> Story, won't you?]
“I'll······ have to think about that a little.”
[Why? Our Story is the best! The others don't even compare!]
She was certainly right. ‘Messiah's Path’ had the highest Status among resurrection Stories. But there was a problem.
“If I choose that Story, I'll lose something precious.”
[Huh? Oh. Y-you're right. If you choose our Story, you'll become a eunuch······. That won't do.]
I hadn't expected to convince her, but surprisingly, Uriel was deeply shaken, as though it concerned her personally. Was me becoming a eunuch that big a problem for Uriel? Why?

[Wh-what do I do? Metatron said that if I don't bring Kim Dokja back, he'll ban me from the internet for a month······ But if I bring him back, Kim Dokja will become a eunuch······ And then······ Oh, wait. Even if he's a eunuch, if I just change his position a little······?]
······What position?
[O-okay! Kim Dokja! Don't worry too much about the eunuch problem. I'll find some way to······!]
Uriel had the look of someone who'd reached some momentous resolution all on her own.
I shook my head firmly.
“I don't want to be a eunuch.”
[Right! So I'll make it okay even if you become one······!]
“Next.”
Several more constellations came to see me after that.
There were representatives from places like <Tamna> and <Guiok>, unaffiliated constellations, and Historical-grade constellations who'd simply come to see me.

The Korean Peninsula's Historical-grade constellations, in particular, left me various words of encouragement before departing. They didn't seem pleased at the prospect of me forming ties with a particular nebula.
[You are the hope of our world.]
[Please don't waver in your resolve.]
I understood how they felt.
The Historical-grade constellations, who had lived under harassment from Narrative-grades ever since becoming constellations, must have deeply envied the way I acted as I pleased.
Before long, the negotiation period ended.
The incarnations took the platform one by one.
It was time to consider the Stories they'd been offered and decide which to inherit.
―Now, let's announce the inheritance results! First, America's ‘Selena Kim’!
The dokkaebi on the platform was as excited as a home-shopping host.
Of course it would be happy.
The Bureau would rake in another enormous haul of coins through this banquet.
―‘Selena Kim’ has chosen to inherit the Story ‘Indomitable Aegis’, bestowed by the constellation ‘Last Conscience’!
Wooooo!
So Selena Kim had chosen <Olympus>, as expected······.
‘Indomitable Aegis’ was a fitting Story for her to choose as the King's Guardian.
As the proceedings continued, my thoughts grew more tangled.
Choose someone, and I'd make enemies.
Choose no one, and I'd make even more.
‘Think carefully. Must this really be a matter of making someone your enemy?’
That was what Persephone had said.
I had a vague grasp of what she meant.
She probably meant that I should embrace all the ‘resurrection Stories’.
I had more than one life, and there would be those who wanted me to inherit their Stories at my next resurrection, too.
But there was still a problem.
<Eden> and <Vedas> certainly wouldn't yield the ‘first resurrection’. Moreover, if I ‘directly inherited’ their Stories, I would surely be subjected to restrictions binding me to them.
There was no getting around it.
The relationship between an incarnation and a constellation was unfair from the start.
Wait. ‘Fair’······?
At last, Yoo Joonghyuk stood and went to the platform.
―The next to inherit a Story is Seoul's Supreme King······.

As Yoo Joonghyuk moved, I heard people in the audience swallowing. The Narrative-grade constellations' gazes were especially strange. Those determined to have Yoo Joonghyuk. And those who, on the other hand, seemed afraid······.
Suddenly, an idea came to me.
And Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
Dionysus had told me to trust no one. But that applied when the other party was a ‘constellation’.
At least here, I had one person—one ‘being I could trust’.
I ran up onto the platform.
Then I grabbed the bewildered Yoo Joonghyuk's hand and raised it high in the air.
“I have something to tell you all.”
I spoke as I turned to the audience. The startled constellations.
I could also see Uriel, who looked on the verge of fainting at the sight of us.
I slowly surveyed the constellations.
The inheritance ceremony was unfair because Story inheritance took the form of one-sided ‘sponsorship’.
Something that happened because constellations and incarnations were never equals.
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ pays attention to your words!]
Narrative-grades looked down on Historical-grades because their power differed, and nebulas looked down on constellations because those in a nebula belonged to a collective.
[The nebula <Vedas> pays attention to your words!]
“‘We’ have decided not to inherit your Stories.”
An immense silence swept over the audience. Formidable gazes poured down on Yoo Joonghyuk and me, exerting pressure. Yoo Joonghyuk, whose hand I was holding, was trembling and glaring at me.
I grinned at him, then spoke to the constellations.
“‘We’ will buy your Stories.”
To make an unfair game fair, the first step was to stand on equal footing with the other side.
“If you want to sell Stories to Yoo Joonghyuk and me, do business with our ‘nebula’.”
